marks.text: This chapter argues that the love is misplaced: past a point, every extra percent of utilization buys a disproportionate amount of waiting.
marks.why: The chapter's thesis: the rest of it measures how steep that curve gets and what to do about it.

marks.text: At 90 percent utilization the average wait is nine times the work itself; at 95 percent it is nineteen times.
marks.why: The numbers that make the thesis concrete, and the ones the later advice on WIP limits leans on.

marks.text: Utilization is only half the story; the other half is variability.
marks.why: Turns the argument: waiting has two causes, so cutting load alone is not enough.
Queue time approximated as a utilization term times a variability term times the mean service time.

marks.text: If waiting is the price of busyness, slack is not waste.
marks.why: The practical conclusion the chapter builds to, and the idea the next chapter's WIP limits put to work.
Capacity held in reserve for work nobody can predict; the chapter's answer to the trap.
